questions.q: Which of the following is an **input** device?
questions.solution: A **scanner** converts a paper document into digital data flowing **into** the computer. The other three all receive data from it.
questions.shortcut: Data in = input. Plotters, monitors, speakers push data out.

questions.q: The shortcut to insert today's date as a fixed value in a cell is —
questions.solution: **Ctrl+; stamps today's date** (fixed text). Ctrl+D fills down — the planted trap.

questions.q: **PARAM 8000**, delivered in 1991, made India one of the few countries able to build supercomputers. It was developed by —
questions.solution: **PARAM 8000** (1991) was built by **C-DAC** (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing), Pune, set up in 1988 after the USA refused to sell India a Cray supercomputer.
questions.shortcut: PARAM = C-DAC, Pune. Not ISRO, not BARC.

questions.q: A MAC address is a —
options: 48-bit physical address fixed by the manufacturer
questions.solution: **MAC = 48 bits, burnt into the NIC**; 32-bit logical describes an IPv4 address.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The gardener is watering the plants.
options: The plants are watered by the gardener.
The plants are being watered by the gardener.
The plants are being water by the gardener.
The plants is being watered by the gardener.
questions.solution: Present continuous → **are being + V3** with the plural new subject 'the plants'. B uses V1; C fails number agreement (is for plants); D drops 'being', turning it into simple present.
questions.shortcut: are being + V3 — check the V3 and the number both.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The two families **know** each other since 1998.
questions.solution: *Since 1998* + still true → **have known**. 'Knew' detaches the fact from the present; 'are knowing' is not a stative use.

questions.q: With which of the following statements would the author most likely agree?
options: Brochures and ceremonies are the best way to clean a lake
Stopping sewage from entering the lake matters more than publicity events
The lake cannot be cleaned by any means
Consultants should be paid more for their work
questions.solution: The author contrasts spending on brochures with the unbuilt drain and says a single drain can surely be afforded. He believes real work (diverting sewage) matters more than publicity. The second option is the reverse; the third is pessimism he does not show — he thinks one drain is affordable; consultants' pay is not discussed.
questions.shortcut: The author's opinion sits in the last line; pick the option that restates it at the same strength.
questions.passage: Every few years the city announces a grand plan to clean its lake. Consultants are hired, glossy brochures are printed, and a minister arrives to plant a sapling on the bank. Then the cameras leave. The sewage pipes that empty into the water are never diverted, the encroachments on the shore are never removed, and the lake grows a little greener each summer. Surely a city that can spend crores on brochures can find the money to lay a single drain.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

The guard said to us, "Please show your ID cards."
options: The guard ordered us to show our ID cards.
The guard requested us showing our ID cards.
The guard requested us to show our ID cards.
The guard requested to us that show our ID cards.
questions.solution: Please marks a request: **requested us to show our ID cards.** The listener sits directly after requested (never 'to us'); the verb after to stays in base form. 'Ordered us' hardens a polite plea into a command; 'requested us showing' swaps the infinitive for a gerund.

questions.q: The English merchant **Ralph Fitch** travelled in India during the reign of —
questions.solution: **Ralph Fitch** (1583–91) was the first English merchant-traveller to describe Mughal India — he came in **Akbar's** reign, decades before Roe.
questions.shortcut: Fitch before the Company: Akbar's time.

questions.q:
Consider the statements:
1. The Fifth Plan was terminated before its full term.
2. Annual plans were also used in 1990-92.
3. The Plan Holiday followed the Second Plan.
Which are correct?
questions.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — the 5th plan was cut short in 1978 and annual plans ran in 1990-92. Statement 3 is wrong: the Plan Holiday followed the **Third** plan (1966-69).

questions.q:
Consider the statements about the President's election:
1. Nominated members of the Rajya Sabha can vote.
2. Members of State Legislative Councils cannot vote.
3. Election disputes are decided by the Election Commission.
Which are correct?
questions.solution: Statement 2 alone is right. Nominated MPs **cannot** vote (statement 1 wrong); disputes go to the **Supreme Court** under Article 71, not the Election Commission (statement 3 wrong).
questions.shortcut: Only elected members vote; SC decides disputes.

questions.q: The largest volcano of the solar system, **Olympus Mons**, is on which planet?
questions.solution: **Olympus Mons** rises on **Mars**, the 'Red Planet' (its colour comes from iron-oxide dust). Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos.

questions.q: A milkman sells a milk-water mixture (milk : water = 8:1) at the marked price which is 12.5% above the cost of milk. His gain per cent is:
questions.solution: Cost per sold litre $= \frac{8}{9}$ of milk's CP; SP $= 1.125 \times$ CP → net $= 1.125 \times \frac{9}{8} - 1 = \frac{81}{64} - 1 = 26.5625\%$.
questions.shortcut: The water is free, so the effective cost per sold litre falls below the milk price.

questions.q: A ladder $17$ m long leans against a vertical wall, its foot $8$ m from the base of the wall. How high does the ladder reach?
questions.shortcut: 8-15-17 family: $15$ m. Trap: $13$ m (grabbed the 5-12-13 family).

questions.q: Two co-interior angles between parallel lines are in the ratio $2:3$. The difference between the two angles is:
questions.solution:
Let the angles be $2k$ and $3k$: $2k+3k=180 \Rightarrow k=36^\circ$.

Angles $72^\circ$ and $108^\circ$; difference $=36^\circ$.

questions.q: A sum amounts to ₹4,840 in 2 years at 10% per annum compound interest. The sum is:
Pointing to a man, Deepak said, **"He is the only son of my father."** How is the man related to Deepak?
questions.solution: Deepak is male, and his father has exactly one son — Deepak. So the man in the photo is **Deepak himself**. The question is a mirror, not a family puzzle.
questions.shortcut: 'Only son of my father' + male speaker = the speaker.

questions.q: Select the pair that fills both blanks: **? : Kitten :: Dog : ?**
questions.solution: Both sides must read **adult : young**. Cat : Kitten ✓ and Dog : Puppy ✓. Kennel is a home and bark a sound, so those options break the link.

questions.solution: 4 appears with 1 and 2 (view 1), 3 and 1 (view 2), 5 and 3 (view 3). So 4 is adjacent to 1, 2, 3 and 5. The only face never seen with 4 is **6**, which must be opposite.

questions.q: Which word comes **first** in the dictionary?
questions.solution: All share MAR. 4th letters: b (Marble), k (Market), g (Margin). b is earliest → **Marble** comes first.
questions.shortcut: Ignore the shared part; only the first differing letter votes.
